extracted.subtask_description: Exposition and results about the j-function, modular polynomials, Weber functions, and applications to complex multiplication and the class number one problem. Contains definitions, transformation properties, arithmetic properties, and proofs used to generate ring class fields and classify imaginary quadratic fields with class number one.

rubrics_metrics.name: q-expansion of the j-function (Theorem 5.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: j(τ) = 1/q + 744 + 196884 q + ··· = 1/q + Σ_{n=0}^∞ c_n q^n where c_n ∈ Z for all n ≥ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows j(τ) is holomorphic on H, invariant under SL2(Z), and has an integral q-expansion at infinity; proof referenced to [11] §4.1. Explains why the factor 1728 appears in the definition of the j-invariant (to make q-expansion coefficients integers without common divisors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular functions for Γ0(m) are generated by j(τ) and j(mτ) (Theorem 5.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: For positive integer m, j(τ) and j(mτ) are modular functions for Γ0(m), and every modular function for Γ0(m) is a rational function of j(τ) and j(mτ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In particular, for SL2(Z) every modular function is a rational function in j(τ). Reference: [6] pp.226–231.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holomorphic at infinity (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A modular function is holomorphic at infinity if its q-expansion does not involve any negative powers of q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to distinguish growth/behavior at cusps and to apply Lemma 5.16 about polynomials in j(τ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma: constantness of holomorphic modular functions (Lemma 5.16(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: A holomorphic modular function for SL2(Z) which is holomorphic at infinity is constant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to deduce structural constraints on modular functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma: holomorphic modular functions are polynomials in j(τ) (Lemma 5.16(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A holomorphic modular function for SL2(Z) is a polynomial in j(τ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from invariance and growth conditions; used to show coefficients of modular polynomials lie in C[j(τ)].

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of the modular polynomial Φ_m(X,Y) (Definition 5.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Φ_m(X,τ) = ∏_{i=1}^{|C(m)|} (X - j(m γ_i τ)), and Φ_m(X,Y) is the polynomial in X,Y obtained by expressing coefficients as polynomials in j(τ). Equivalently Φ_m(X,j(τ)) = ∏_{σ∈C(m)} (X - j(σ τ)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C(m) = set of matrices (a b; 0 d) with ad=m, a>0, 0≤b<d, gcd(a,b,d)=1; coefficients are symmetric polynomials in the j(mγ_i τ)'s, SL2(Z)-invariant, and meromorphic at infinity hence polynomials in j(τ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic properties of Φ_m(X,Y) (Theorem 5.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) Φ_m(X,Y) ∈ Z[X,Y]. (ii) Φ_m(X,Y) is irreducible as a polynomial in X. (iii) Φ_m(X,Y)=Φ_m(Y,X) if m>1. (iv) For prime p, Φ_p(X,Y) ≡ (X^p − Y)(X − Y^p) (mod p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These properties follow from properties of the j-function; proofs referenced to [6] pp.231–234.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclic sublattice (Definition 5.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: A cyclic sublattice Λ' ⊂ Λ of index m is a sublattice with [Λ:Λ'] = m and Λ/Λ' cyclic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to relate values of the modular polynomial to lattice inclusions (Theorem 5.20).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular polynomial and lattices correspondence (Theorem 5.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: For positive integer m and complex numbers u,v, Φ_m(u,v)=0 iff there exists a lattice Λ and a cyclic sublattice Λ' of index m with j(Λ')=u and j(Λ)=v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relates algebraic equation Φ_m(u,v)=0 to geometric lattice data; used in complex multiplication arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primitive ideal (Definition 5.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: A proper ideal a of an order O is primitive if it is not of the form d·a' with integer d>1 and proper ideal a'. An element α∈O is primitive if α≠dβ for d>1, β∈O.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primitivity characterizes which ideals give cyclic sublattices (Lemma 5.22).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primitive ideals correspond to cyclic sublattices (Lemma 5.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let O be an imaginary quadratic order and b a proper fractional ideal. For a proper ideal a, ab is a sublattice of b of index N(a), and ab is cyclic iff a is primitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses exact sequence 0→b/ab→O/ab→O/b→0 and the structure theorem for finite abelian groups; applied to principal ideals αO gives criterion in terms of primitive elements α.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Main Theorem of Complex Multiplication (Theorem 5.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let O be an order in an imaginary quadratic field K and a a proper fractional ideal of O. Then j(a) is an algebraic integer and K(j(a)) is the ring class field of O.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central CM theorem linking j-invariants of ideals to abelian extensions (ring class fields).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hilbert class field via j(OK) (Corollary 5.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: For imaginary quadratic field K, K(j(OK)) is the Hilbert class field of K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows since Hilbert class field is the ring class field of OK (apply Theorem 5.23).

rubrics_metrics.name: Frobenius action on j-invariants (Theorem 5.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let O be an order in imaginary quadratic K and L its ring class field. For a proper fractional ideal a of O and a prime ideal p of OK, Frob_p(j(a)) = j((p ∩ O)·a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives explicit Galois/Frobenius action on special values of j; leads directly to ideal-class-to-Galois isomorphism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideal class group ≅ Galois group action on j (Corollary 5.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The map Cl(O) → Gal(L/K), a ↦ σ_a where σ_a: j(b) ↦ j(ab), is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restatement of Theorem 5.25 in terms of class field theory; identifies Gal(L/K) with the class group via action on j-values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and normalization of γ2(τ) (start of §6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define γ2(τ) as the unique cube root of j(τ) which is holomorphic and real-valued on the imaginary axis (chosen via cube root of Δ(τ)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: γ2(τ) is used because it has nicer arithmetic properties at CM points; existence of unique cube root follows from nonvanishing of Δ(τ) on H and reality on imaginary axis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algebraicity of γ2 at CM points (Theorem 6.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For discriminant D of order O = [1,τ0] in imaginary quadratic K (with specified τ0), γ2(τ0) is an algebraic integer and K(γ2(τ0)) is the ring class field corresponding to O. Moreover Q(γ2(τ0)) = Q(j(τ0)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A refinement of CM theory showing small roots of j generate the same class fields; reference to [6] pp.249–255 for proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weber functions f, f1, f2 (definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Weber functions defined by q-product expansions: f(τ)=q^{-1/48} ∏_{n=1}^∞ (1+q^{n-1/2}), f1(τ)=q^{-1/48} ∏_{n=1}^∞ (1−q^{n-1/2}), f2(τ)=√2 q^{-1/24} ∏_{n=1}^∞ (1+q^n), with q^{1/2}:=e^{π i τ}. They are derived from the Dedekind η-function η(τ)=q^{1/24} ∏_{n=1}^∞ (1−q^n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These product expansions lead to identities relating f,f1,f2 and η used later to produce class fields and compute special values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identities among Weber functions and η (equations (6.1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: f(τ)f1(τ)f2(τ)=√2 η(τ) (and related identities f1(2τ)f2(τ)=2^{1/2} η(2τ) etc. as in (6.1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful product expansions and transformation relations that enable arithmetic evaluations of γ2 and j.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formulas for γ2 and Δ in terms of Weber/η (Theorem 6.2)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These relations give efficient means to compute j-values and show q-expansions of γ2 and j have integer coefficients; used to prove Theorem 5.14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformation properties of η and Weber functions (Proposition 6.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: η(τ+1)=ζ_{24} η(τ); η(−1/τ)=√(−iτ) η(τ) (with chosen square root positive on imaginary axis). Also f(τ+1)=ζ_{48}^{-1} f1(τ), f1(τ+1)=ζ_{48}^{-1} f(τ), f2(τ+1)=ζ_{24} f2(τ); under τ→−1/τ: f(−1/τ)=f(τ), f1(−1/τ)=f2(τ), f2(−1/τ)=f1(τ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof for η given; Weber transformation properties follow from definitions and η-transformations; crucial for relating values at CM points under modular transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small powers of Weber functions generate ring class fields (Theorem 6.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For positive integer m with 3 ∤ m and m ≡ 3 (mod 4), and O = [1, (1+√−m)/2] an order in K = Q(√−m), certain small powers of f evaluated at CM points (e.g. f(τ0)^2) are algebraic integers and K(f(τ0)^2) is the ring class field of O.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A special case of Weber/Birch results: Weber gave many such theorems showing that small combinations/powers of f,f1,f2 generate class fields (see [15], modern proof by Birch [3]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete list of imaginary quadratic fields with class number one (Theorem 6.5)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the resolution of the class number one problem via Heegner's proof (presented following Stark's exposition); combines CM, Weber functions, and Diophantine analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diophantine constraint used in Heegner argument (Proposition 6.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: The only integer solutions to 2X(X^3+1)=Y^2 are (X,Y)=(0,0),(−1,0),(1,±2),(2,±6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof proceeds by factoring in various UFDs (Z[i], Z[ω], Z[√−2]) and analysis of cases, then an infinite-descent-style argument for remaining case; the finite set of solutions yields the finite list of p leading to class number one.

rubrics_metrics.name: j-invariant determines imaginary quadratic field (argument around (6.15)-(6.18))
rubrics_metrics.description: If j(OK)=j(OK') then OK and OK' are homothetic lattices which forces the underlying fields to be equal; hence j(OK) determines K uniquely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to argue that computed γ2/j values for the six primes correspond to distinct imaginary quadratic fields; supports final classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dirichlet class number formula (Theorem 7.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let D<0 be a fundamental discriminant and χ mod D an odd real primitive Dirichlet character. Then L(1,χ) = 2π h(D) / (w √|D|), where w=2 for D<−4, w=4 for D=−4, w=6 for D=−3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit analytic relation connecting L-values to class numbers; foundational for analytic approaches to class number growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hecke's conditional growth bound for class numbers (Theorem 7.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If L(s,χ) ≠ 0 for real s > 1 − c/log|D| (χ as above), then h(D) > c1 √|D| / log|D| for absolute constants c,c1>0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under GRH-type zero-free region hypotheses for Dirichlet L-functions, one gets effective lower bounds for class numbers; implies h(D)→∞ conditional on GRH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deuring's result supporting Gauss' conjecture under RH falsity (Theorem 7.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the classical Riemann hypothesis is false, then h(D)→∞ for −D sufficiently large.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An unexpected conditional result showing either truth or falsity of RH yields class number growth; combined with Hecke gives unconditional result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heilbronn's conditional result (Theorem 7.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the generalized Riemann hypothesis is false, then h(D)→∞ as D→−∞.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributes to the Hecke–Deuring–Heilbronn trichotomy argument proving h(D)→∞ unconditionally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hecke–Deuring–Heilbronn unconditional growth theorem (Theorem 7.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: h(D)→∞ as D→−∞ (unconditional conclusion reached by combining Hecke, Deuring, Heilbronn results).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates one of the first proofs that consider both possibilities (RH true or false) to deduce the same arithmetic consequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gauss' problems on class numbers (Conjecture 7.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three conjectures by Gauss: (1) h(D)→∞ as D→−∞; (2) lists of imaginary quadratic fields with small given class number are complete; (3) infinitely many real quadratic fields have class number one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context and historical motivation for class number investigations; parts (1) and (2) have substantial progress/theorems, (3) remains open.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coates' conjecture on cyclotomic Z_p-extensions (Conjecture 7.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: For F=Q and p arbitrary prime, conjecture that h(O_{F_n})=1 for all n ≥ 1 (where F_n are layers in the cyclotomic Z_p-extension).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relates class number one problems to behavior in Z_p-extensions and cyclotomic fields; motivates computational and Iwasawa-theoretic approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture (Conjecture 7.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: If rank_Z E(Q)=g for an elliptic curve E/Q, then L(E,s) has a zero of order g at s=1 and L(E,s) ∼ c_E (s−1)^g for some nonzero constant c_E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a link between ranks of elliptic curves and special values/orders of vanishing of Hasse–Weil L-functions; relevant to analytic lower bounds for class numbers via elliptic curves.
